title: Canada Police Recruitment 2026: RCMP Requirements & Steps
metaDescription: Complete 2026 guide to joining the RCMP in Canada. Age, citizenship, fitness test, 26-week Depot training, pay, and the seven-step application process.
headline: Join the RCMP: Complete 2026 Canada Police Recruitment Guide

sections.title: Who Can Apply to the RCMP
sections.content:
To join the Royal Canadian Mounted Police as a regular member, you must be a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident. Permanent residents need at least 1,095 days of physical presence in Canada during the last five years. You must be at least 18 years old to apply and 19 to be hired, and there is no upper age limit.

You also need a Canadian secondary school diploma or an accepted equivalent, a valid unrestricted Canadian driver's licence, and functional proficiency in English or French. Applicants must be willing to relocate anywhere in Canada, work shifts, carry a firearm, and complete 26 weeks of residential training at Depot in Regina, Saskatchewan.

sections.title: The Seven-Step Selection Process
sections.content:
The RCMP selection process has seven steps: an online application through GC Jobs, an online career presentation and entrance assessment, an applicant fitness test and attribute interview, forms and documents, a suitability interview, psychological and medical assessments, and a field investigation and security assessment. Candidates who clear all seven steps receive a troop offer for Depot.

The full process currently takes about 12 to 18 months for most applicants. The RCMP's National Recruitment Strategy 2026-2029 aims to cut the average timeline to about six months by 2028-2029, and applicants in British Columbia and Yukon already move faster through Project Red Serge.

sections.title: Fitness, Medical and Character Standards
sections.content:
All applicants must pass the Physical Fitness Assessment, which replaced the old PARE test in April 2024. The assessment tests strength, endurance and job-related movement, so regular running, strength training and core work before applying make a real difference. Vision, hearing, psychological and medical standards are also checked.

Character matters just as much as fitness. Criminal history, recent illegal activity, dishonesty during the process, active bankruptcy or a dishonourable discharge can end an application or trigger a deferral. Being screened out at any stage usually means a six-month wait before reapplying.

sections.title: Training, Pay and Career Paths
sections.content:
Cadets spend 26 weeks at Depot Division in Regina, Saskatchewan, where accommodation, meals, uniforms and travel are covered. As of April 1, 2026, cadets receive $1,000 per week during training. After graduation, constables start on a stepped pay scale that rises with years of service.

The RCMP offers more than 150 specialized career paths after Depot, including major crimes, cybercrime, forensics, aviation, marine services, federal policing and community policing. Officers can also work toward instructor, investigator and leadership roles over a full career.

faqs.q: How old do you need to be to join the RCMP?
faqs.a: You must be at least 18 years old to apply to the RCMP and at least 19 years old to be hired as a regular member. There is no upper age limit, and applicants in their thirties, forties and fifties have successfully joined, provided they meet the physical, medical and character standards.

faqs.q: Do you need a university degree to become an RCMP officer?
faqs.a: No, a university degree is not required to become an RCMP constable. The minimum education requirement is a Canadian secondary school diploma or a recognized equivalent. Post-secondary education is preferred by some recruiters and can strengthen an application, but it is not mandatory. What matters most is meeting the citizenship, age, licence, fitness, medical and character requirements.

faqs.q: How long does RCMP training take?
faqs.a: RCMP training at Depot Division in Regina, Saskatchewan lasts 26 weeks and is fully residential. Cadets receive one thousand dollars per week during training, with accommodation, meals, uniforms and travel covered. The program covers law, firearms, driving, physical training, scenario-based policing and community relations. Graduates are then posted to a detachment anywhere in Canada.

faqs.q: What is the RCMP fitness test?
faqs.a: Applicants must pass the Physical Fitness Assessment, which replaced the older PARE test in April 2024. It measures strength, endurance and job-related physical ability through a series of stations. Regular running, strength training and core exercises in the months before applying give candidates the best chance of passing on the first attempt.
